text:
incidentbot: Pager: HIGH_RATE auth_failures on proxy-svc (alert id: A-20260320-77). 401 spikes from svc-proxy-*/us-west-2. Graph: https://alerts.internal/r/A-20260320-77 :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): Oncall here — I’m looking. Any customer impact reported yet?
incidentbot: Alert details -> 401s/sec peaked ~3k, correlated with svc-proxy traffic to external indexer (10.4.8.0/24). No high-severity customer pages flagged yet.
eli (sre): Seeing repeated token-reuse patterns from service account svc-proxy-sa. Sample log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T14:12:03Z svc-proxy-12 auth=fail token_id=AAAA.. reused_from=10.4.8.22
2026-03-20T14:12:05Z svc-proxy-07 auth=fail token_id=AAAA.. src_ip=34.120.7.19
```
sam (eng): If tokens are being replayed, we should rotate svc-proxy keys immediately and block egress to the suspected IP range. I can run the rotate script — will coordinate with oncall.
maya (oncall): Do it. Temp egress block + rotate. @emily (cust-succ) start drafting a customer note (we'll confirm impact). @lee (security) loop legal if we confirm leaked creds.
ops-bot: Executing playbook -> `block-egress --cidr 34.120.7.0/24`
ops-bot: Done: egress to 34.120.7.0/24 blocked on prod-proxy NACLs and host iptables.
sam (eng): Running rotation: `./scripts/rotate-service-key svc-proxy-sa --rotate-kms`
sam (eng): Rotation output: key replaced, new key id = rk-9f3b, old key disabled for immediate use. Rolling restart svc-proxy pods to pick up new creds.
lee (security): Created ticket INC-4382, adding CISO/legal and tagging compliance. Recommendation: full keystore rotation for affected scopes + S3/Kinesis audit for possible forwards.
emily (cust-succ): Drafting a short note: "We are investigating anomalous authentication activity affecting some internal service accounts. No confirmed customer data access as of now. We will update within 30 minutes." Will post after we validate impact.
eli (sre): Quick forensics: I see a staging-forwarder config that forwarded debug logs to a third-party indexer; the forwarder had an IAM role allowing log read. Quarantining forwarder now.
sam (eng): Quarantine done — disabled forwarder job and revoked its role. Rolling back any recent forwarder config changeets to last-known-good.
maya (oncall): Run smoke tests and tail auth logs; report 401 trend.
ops-bot: Smoke tests: 3/4 endpoints OK, spike on /v1/infer reduced but intermittent 401s remain (~30/min).
sam (eng): Those intermittent 401s look like cached, pre-rotation tokens hitting edge caches. Flushing auth cache across edge nodes: `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n "systemctl restart auth-cache"; done`
ops-bot: Auth cache flush complete. 401s dropping to baseline (~2/min).
eli (sre): No evidence of customer data outbound to public buckets. Suspected leak was limited to internal debug logs forwarded to vendor indexer; vendor has been contacted to sweep and delete any retained samples. Forensics: saving log bundle to secure bucket s3://sec-incident-3141609999 for analysis.
lee (security): We'll schedule KMS rewrap for the next maintenance window and follow up with compliance for potential notification requirements. Legal looped in.
emily (cust-succ): Updated customer note posted to status page: "Mitigated — rotating internal service credentials; no confirmed customer data exposure. We'll share follow-up"
maya (oncall): Summary/next steps: 1) Mitigated live (egress block + rotation + forwarder quarantine), 2) Follow-up: full keystore rotation (sam), KMS rewrap (lee), customer comms (emily), forensic deep-dive (eli). Marking incident as mitigated for paging. :white_check_mark:
sam (eng): I'll write the keystore rotation runbook and start the full rotation plan. ETA doc in 2h.
eli (sre): Forensics note: capture retained logs, timeline, and IP list. I’ll hand to security for any regulatory review.
lee (security): Noted. Filing evidence package and estimated regulatory window.
maya (oncall): Great work — please add action items to INC-4382 and we’ll do a postmortem tomorrow. Closing page but keeping incident channel open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
